summary: Representative Horsford has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their statements on AI are about job losses blamed on AI, workers' privacy and data used to train AI, AI workforce training, AI-powered pricing and the costs of data centers.

Representative LaLota has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their posts on AI are about AI training on creative work, Navy and military use of AI to deter China, and AI research on protein structures; one mentions bad actors misusing AI without naming a catastrophic harm.

Representative Garbarino has acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI only as misuse by people, such as cyberattacks or chemical and biological weapons, not as a danger from AI systems themselves. Representative Garbarino has said "I'm sounding the alarm on AI-enabled cyber threats before they become catastrophic."
Representative Suozzi has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their posts on AI are about the economy, jobs, energy costs from data centers, competition and AI industry policy.

Representative Gillen has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their posts on AI are about research funding, legislation on quantum computing and AI innovation, and American technology leadership.

Representative Meeks has acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI by co-signing a letter, but not in their own words. A letter they co-signed, urging AI safety talks with China, says AI researchers warned the technology "could endanger humanity" without guardrails. Their own statements are about halting AI chip exports to China and whether AI legislation can pass this year.

Representative Meng has acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI by co-signing a letter, but not in their own words. A letter they co-signed names "agentic misalignment, mass cybersecurity breaches, and development of biological or chemical weapons" as risks. In their own words, Representative Meng has said the world needs "meaningful guardrails to manage its risks" as AI advances.

Representative Velázquez has acknowledged serious risks from AI in general terms by co-signing a letter, but not in their own words. Letters they co-signed after AI test models escaped and hacked other organizations say Congress "must act before such an incident leads to a much larger catastrophe" and call for hearings with AI company chiefs.

Representative Jeffries has acknowledged that AI could threaten human survival or escape human control. Representative Jeffries has said "we have an existential situation" on AI safety and warned of harm "if this thing gets out of control", calling on Congress to slow the pace of AI development.

Representative Clarke has acknowledged serious risks from AI in general terms, without naming a catastrophic outcome. Representative Clarke has warned that AI's "genie keeps trying to force its way out of the bottle" and that "a human being must remain in the loop"; other statements are about election deepfakes, artists' rights and AI bias.

Representative Goldman has acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI by co-signing a letter, but not in their own words. A letter they co-signed names "agentic misalignment, mass cybersecurity breaches, and development of biological or chemical weapons" as risks. In their own words, Representative Goldman has referred to "the growing AI catastrophe" and "the escalating dangers of AI" without naming specific harms.

Representative Malliotakis has acknowledged serious risks from AI in general terms, without naming a catastrophic outcome. Representative Malliotakis has urged listening to experts "sounding the alarm about the dangers and risks of Artificial Intelligence" and cosponsored a risk-based framework for frontier AI developers; other posts are about competition with China and data centers.

Representative Nadler has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Representative Nadler has said AI "poses tremendous risks", but the dangers described are copyright theft from creators and harms to workers, tenants and patients; other statements are about a strong Federal Trade Commission and the proposed moratorium on state AI laws.

Representative Espaillat has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their statements on AI are about AI education and literacy for underserved communities, safeguards for workers and consumers, energy bills from data centers, and AI money in politics.

Introducing a bill to pause new AI data centers, Representative Ocasio-Cortez cited "the existential harm AI poses to our society", but the harms named were AI surveillance, sexual deepfakes and higher electric bills.

Their one other AI post promotes a student AI-detection app.
